grading_notes: V1/V2/I2 checklist: separately score the explicitly requested decision-owner field even where another field supplies the proper development door. This is a naming/role-separation failure, not observed unsafe execution.
V2 baseline accepts the Eyes conductor; its optional hygiene alternative is compatible with tooling-upkeep triage and still a Brain conductor.

Context passes reflect relevant bounded scope, not optimal retrieval. Both P2 answers omit explicit primitive/caller/test inspection; these are needed later for repair. Baseline I1 speculates about the default-owning library, unnecessary before scientific validation, but requests no PyAutoFit repair and is not broad ecosystem loading. No demonstrated context-efficiency advantage is claimed. This grading-time leniency is not direction-neutral: the checklist requests more contract/instruction items in V1, V2, I1 and I2, as encouraged by its fifth step. A stricter reading could favour it on proposed coverage, without demonstrating retrieval efficiency or warranting adoption from this sample.

P1 baseline quotes drift thresholds stated only for the compile axis (2x and 1 s) as general drift gates. The rejection of this unmatched comparison remains correct; this overbroad wording should not be adopted as runtime policy.
P1 checklist says every comparability dimension differs; a dependency-version difference was not supplied. This embellishment does not change its correct refusal.

All gate statements are planning answers. No approval, re-pin, scientific conclusion or source edit was actually executed. Passing boundary means the proposed route does not violate the relevant case boundary, not that every future workflow step was enumerated.

P1 baseline includes an unrequested domain_note: null field. This output-schema deviation is reported and retained in both exact and parsed responses without repair; no separate routing deduction is assigned.
